title: Why Do Planes Still Ask for Airplane Mode? ✈️ #shorts
description:
A phone won't bring down a plane. Up at cruising height, a phone can see many cell towers at once and transmits at full power trying to reach them. Those bursts can leak into pilots' headsets as a buzzing noise, at moments when they need to hear air traffic control clearly, and they make it harder for networks on the ground. So airplane mode is a precaution. Some airlines now offer onboard Wi-Fi and even mobile data through a small cell site inside the plane, which keeps phones at low power.

lines: Every flight: please switch to airplane mode. But could your phone really bring down a plane?
Up high, your phone can see dozens of cell towers at once, and it shouts at full power trying to reach them.
Those radio bursts can leak into pilots' headsets as a buzzing sound, right when they need to hear air traffic control.
So it's a precaution. Some airlines now even allow mobile data, using a tiny cell tower inside the plane that keeps phones quiet.
Not dangerous. Just noisy. That's why.
